notes.text: The opening continues a preceding discussion: it states the nonempty intersection of the two negative parts, repeats the written equality-sign shorthand before si, and argues by the excluded identity of two binary decompositions. It ends by saying the two positive parts are uniquely determined. This is an account of the manuscript argument. No independent proof check was undertaken.

The two inclusion chains have the five labels Sigma1+, E1, Sigma12, E2, Sigma2+, with each arrow directed away from its E label. The lower chain sits beneath a single unarrowed segment with three differently shaped ink marks. The NB gives two amalgamation formulas and contains two overwritten characters in its second line.

The oblique annotation begins “Ceci n’implique pas que les quatre ensembles … soient distincts”. It discusses the written cross-equality Sigma1+ = Sigma2-, says “qui équivaut à” before E1 = Sigma12 and “entraîne” before E2 = empty set, then gives the parenthetical set-difference formulas. The words “On ne veut pas exclure ce cas” are legible. The last lines contain the interlinear “deux décomp. bin.” and cancellations around “sont strictmt”. This reader has not proved the equivalence or any ensuing mathematical claim.

Mathematical context was used only as a reading cue: the paired positive and negative signs help compare local subscripts, the set-difference context supports the crossed-letter X reading, and the repeated inclusion arrows help identify arrowheads and hooks. Context was not used to discard the dot above a minus, the overmark on Sigma, the high oval after a comma, or to complete the cancelled definition’s missing closure.

The lower paragraph proposes studying finite “indicellés” families, with that adjective still uncertain, of pairwise non-parallel binary decompositions. The live family symbol has the capital-Pi form. Several earlier formulas are cancelled. The last sentence ends with the legible word “floppées”, and the status of the heavily retraced “très” remains open.

There is no title, date, or authorial page number visible on this sheet. The light lower-left 26 is recorded only as archive sheet numbering. No explicit request for a proof check or statement of mathematical doubt is visible; the uncertainties reported here concern reading and cancellation state.

workflow_feedback: Read only the assigned brief, page packet, current notation, C/H page witnesses, page context and preamble. Whole image viewed once for layout; each provided half viewed once line by line; nine single crops of the remaining coherent loci, all 3000 px wide with LANCZOS, autocontrast and sharpening. The long slanted note received one crop rotated clockwise 48 degrees. No further recrops, no OCR, no text-layer extraction, no external research, no other page or reader consulted, and no compilation. Some crops necessarily contain crossing horizontal and oblique ink belonging to different loci; each locus received one deep reading. One attempted delivery of crop 09 was omitted by the tool output limit; it was then delivered alone and actually viewed once. The packet’s folder-wide footer mentioning other scans was noticed but supplied no evidence for this reading. Remaining ambiguities are explicit; no mathematical proof check was performed. Mechanical checks confirmed exact witness substrings after whitespace folding, required finding fields, all whole-image bounding rectangles, crop-file presence, and balanced TeX braces. No compilation was run.
